title.description: Short human display name, e.g. "Stats Extraction". THE arena's title everywhere a human sees one — cards, the header switcher, player pages. Distinct from the taxonomy leaf's `name`, which is a long descriptive phrase ("NHST stats + effect-size + CI extraction from manuscripts") better suited to a subtitle. Before this field existed the two lived in different registries — the leaf name in index.json and a hand-maintained short name in the app's lib/config.ts — so a card and the header switcher on the SAME page showed different names for the same arena.

unlisted.description: The reason this arena is kept off the public hub index (leaderboard-app/scripts/lib/listing.mjs). Absent = listed.

runner.description: Run-environment policy (schema v12, framework/container.py). container-required: every player must run in the pinned runner image; a player that cannot is refused before the first task. exemptions-allowed (the default when absent): a player of a NAMED exempt adapter class runs on the host and its env record says isolation host-exempt.

pass_bars.description: Pre-registered pass bars, written and committed BEFORE any player is scored (owner decision 2026-10-14: bars met -> continue; a bar missed -> stop and ask the owner). Evaluated by the arena's tools/check_bars.py against a run.

min_ranked_n.description: Optional (2026-06-13 fairness handoff §E). Minimum size of the COMMON task set every ranked player shares, below which the leaderboard flags the headline ranking 'insufficient sample, not ranked'. Guards tiny synthetic-only splits (e.g. the table arena's 2 docs) from being read as a real ranking.

data_tiers.description: Optional (2026-10-19). Board display per DATA TIER, for a task set that lists one in task_sets/<v>/tiers.jsonl: each tier is its own board, never pooled (framework/data_tiers.py, leaderboard-app/scripts/lib/data-tiers.mjs). Keys are tier ids, in display order. score_label null = the tier publishes no score.

score_term.description: Glossary term id (leaderboard-app/lib/glossary.ts) the tier board's score column uses; default the arena's primary column id.

task_set_versions.description: The version ladder for this arena's task sets. ORDER IS NOT MEANING: which version the leaderboard builds from is decided by `status`, not by position. Before `status` existed, `build-data.mjs::resolveTaskSetVersion` took the LAST entry, so declaring a new version instantly made every run of the previous one invisible with nothing failing.

status.description: `current` = the version new runs go to and the board defaults to. `frozen` = immutable; the generator must reproduce it byte-for-byte (guarded by `framework audit --frozen-drift`) and the runner REFUSES to append run records to it. `superseded` = frozen AND no longer surfaced by default. Omitted on every arena that has only ever had one task set; when NO entry declares a status the legacy last-entry rule applies unchanged.

supersedes.description: The version this one replaces. Its scores are NOT automatically comparable — see `comparable_with_previous`.

generator_fingerprint.description: sha256 over the sorted `task_id -> input_hash` map this version's generator produces. Required in practice on a frozen version: it is the only thing that can catch a generator edit silently rewriting history. Pinning a constant and merely REORDERING two `rng` calls each changed a frozen task set before, and only a diff caught it.

comparable_with_previous.description: False when the gold, the scorer or the primary metric changed, so a reader must NOT diff this version's scores against the previous one's. The leaderboard renders an explicit banner rather than letting the two sit side by side unlabelled.

rationale.description: One sentence, published verbatim on the arena page: why this version exists. A version bump with no stated reason is how a benchmark loses the trust it is built to supply.

rationale_path.description: Path relative to the arena directory (optionally with a #anchor) to the long form, e.g. `CHANGELOG.md#v2`. Rendered on /arenas/<id>/about.

benchmark_splits.description: Optional. Declares the revealed/private dual-benchmark policy for this arena. When present, the generator must accept a `split` argument and emit difficulty-matched 'revealed' and 'private' suites from the same injected-mistake catalog. framework/parity.py verifies they cover the same difficulty x mistake matrix. When absent, the arena is single-suite (legacy behavior; all tasks treated as their declared visibility).

revealed.description: The published suite. Its seed is committed so anyone can reproduce it; its gold and full per-task results are disclosed in the Open Benchmark.

seed.description: Committed generator seed for the revealed split.

private.description: The contamination-protected official suite. Seed is secret; gold is gitignored; findings are redacted at write time.

seed_source.description: Where the private seed comes from. 'secret_file' = a gitignored arenas/<id>/task_sets/<v>/.private_seed; 'env' = the SCIENCEARENA_PRIVATE_SEED environment variable.

real_holdout_dir.description: Optional. Repo-relative dir (gitignored) of hand-curated real-world tasks whose gold is committed only to the eval-only registry; appended to the synthetic private split. PDF arenas point this at their _held_out/ PMC corpus.

match_axes.description: Difficulty-axis ids (subset of difficulty_axes) whose per-cell coverage must match across splits.

match_categories.description: If true, every injected-mistake category (error_categories id / deception kind) present in one split must be present in the other.

count_tolerance.description: Max allowed relative difference in per-cell task counts between splits.

composition_unmatched.description: OPT-IN, per task-set version. Declares that the named versions' revealed and private splits are NOT matched on item-KIND composition, so the gate must not claim they are. The report then prints PARITY PARTIAL, names what it did not enforce, and shows the per-cell composition table. Declared kinds and per-cell task counts are still checked exactly; only the synthesised `clean` residual (a symptom of the same cause) stops being gated. Use this ONLY where measurement shows the generator draws composition from the seed, and put the measurement in `reason`. It is not a tolerance and must not be turned into one.

versions.description: EXHAUSTIVE list of the task-set versions this excuses. A version absent from this list gets the full strict check, which is how the declaration expires: the version that fixes the generator is simply not listed, so no one has to remember to remove anything. Never replace this with a boolean or an open-ended 'until fixed' flag - an exemption premised on transience never expires.

reason.description: Why, with the MEASUREMENT that establishes it, published verbatim in the gate's output. A declaration a reader cannot check is an assertion.

independent_holdout.description: True when the PRIVATE split is a GENUINELY INDEPENDENT corpus (real third-party artifacts under real_holdout_dir) rather than the same generator under a secret seed. Such a split cannot mirror the revealed difficulty grid — real material comes with whatever constructs its authors used, and hand-picking it to fit a template would stop it being a holdout. When true, framework/parity.py skips cell/category matching and reports OK with a note. The revealed split must still be fully symmetric across players; that is what framework audit gates.

error_categories.description: Optional. Failure modes that scorer.score() may report via score.findings[].category. Drives the categorical histogram in tool reports — including for held-out tasks (where per-task content is redacted but category counts survive). Arenas with no error_categories produce shallower reports (summary + ranking only). When benchmark_splits.parity.match_categories is true, this array doubles as the injected-mistake taxonomy that both splits must cover.

display_columns.description: Per-arena leaderboard column manifest. Each entry projects a numeric value out of a run-record and declares how to render it.

task_sets.description: Optional. The task-set versions this column can be populated from. Absent means every version, which is the right default for the arenas with one metric family. Declared when a version changes what the scorer emits: pdf-text-fidelity-v1 v1 publishes levenshtein_similarity/token_f1 while v2 publishes body_recall/body_precision/leak_per_1k_body, and a column that cannot be populated for the version being viewed is noise -- it renders as an em-dash in every row and trains the reader to ignore the table.

tier_pivot.description: Per-arena tier-pivot semantics for the per-tier composite score panel and the tasks-page tier filter.
